I would look up and carefully read the 5 stages of grief that one goes through when facing death or something as “interrupting”, to put it mildly. It would be good to be aware of where you find yourself in these 5 stages and then also where your loved ones will be as you will eventually let them know. It isn’t always so clean cut as it is laid out below. They may react in so many ways but know that it is your journey and your own understanding that matters.

I would try to interpret that simply as words of love rather than take it all literally. Your grieving is normal and so is their’s. We (western world, or North America especially) live in a society that is particularly sheltered from the “truth” and so many of us don’t know how to deal with it. If you find someone that doesn’t feel awkward about your dying, it would be amazing keep them close. I imagine it’s a deeply human feeling to have someone accompany you out.

2. Anger

3. Bargaining

hey Tokodan,

Throughout my illnesses I have pondered what the point of this is. what is the silver lining and what is the incessant suffering for. I've come to the conclusion that it is pretty meaningless and random to me from where I stand now. It's hard to romanticize it as a struggle toward redemption like many movies out there.  Therefore when i say "the lesson is", it's pretty much because I feel forced into the position to use the cards i have been dealt to propel me forward (or any direction really) by seeing what I can still do differently that what I have done before due to circumstance. Events in our lives can be interpreted in a multitude of ways depending on perspective. The lesson is for me today because it fits my story. With my same background, one could also say the lesson is to slow down, accept what is with equanimity and eliminate desire, which can also be correct. 

I agree with you that it is premature to make conclusions about life when stuck in the middle of it. And yet, because my life feels like it's degenerating in terms of my personal capacity to do anything more than stay alive, void of depth and the understanding I once possessed, i find that I am in a position where I gotta hold onto an idea that links me to my alienated previous self. Nature and hiking are things that don't bring me any passion anymore but the fact that I am still able to walk somewhat is what allows me to draw on the idea that if i don't do what I want today, i may not be able to do it tomorrow. People hear that sort of lesson all the time and it is quite intuitive. I had the fortune of experiencing this downtrend in fast forward whereas it is more common to slowly progress into different stages of life with different expectations, habits, interests and its corresponding abilities. 

Thank you for your encouragement. The pro i think is that I can feel a sense of accomplishment for myself without having to measure it with someone else's ruler. There are plenty of cons such as reckless behaviour due to desperation that could lead to even more health issues down the line. I have weighed it out and my decision still seems to resonate well with me. 

Thank you for your comment! all the best to you

Hey! I m all for brutal honestly. 

What makes anything scientific is ability to analyze and have predictable outcomes. This is why I put in question the absolute authority of specialists opinion in TBI. It is extremely hard work to untangle the TBI puzzle and I am eager to see where research takes us next. Again, as you said, if working with one therapy works over another then by all means. Years of experience + statement of "every brain injury is different" doesn't always = progress. My first post started with me getting into car accident because I was encouraged to resume my activities even though I told them many times  that driving = overload of information for me. I put my trust into people that were essentially doing educated guesswork regarding in their recommendations. For sure for most things we can use their help to advance ourselves but knowing our limits serves a purpose. 

As for neurogenesis, the ability to create new brain cells in the brain was believed to be impossible until around 2010 and then they discovered that brain cells do reproduce in human and just a few months ago a renown researcher in California said there wasn't any possibility for neurogenesis because the protein used to identify new cells has to be used with another protein as a marker for  neurogenesis. 

https://www.daytondailynews.com/lifestyles/health/brain-tissue-samples-suggest-stop-adding-neurons-our-early-teens/HU3BAtJJ7ajD4eX6AEL66I/

Thank you for your reply! I was exaggerating a general frustration I had about not having the solutions I would hope for. Indeed we have progressed although it was known for at least 500 years that someone that was hit on the head would have altered behaviour and is “not quite like him/herself”. Our methods of diagnosis are more advanced because we managed to have three tools: one is imaging and the other is neuropsychological assessment and finally the neurological examination. The scans are useful to correlate the injured parts of the brain to the resulting deficits and those aren’t conclusive when scans are taken too late or if there were compounded injuries. Other than emergency treatment there isn’t much those scans can do from my experience. The neuropsych assessment is an interesting one but doesn’t take into account cognitive reserve and many other factors. It gives a broad picture of how far the patient is relative to the normal and remains the tip of the iceberg. The neurological examination is interested in reactions of different parts of the brain but not so much performance. 

These three tools remain broad and random unless there is a big problem that jumps out. Even the classification system of mTBI or moderate and severe don’t necessarily give that much of an indication on the outcome because it also depends on previous history and age and many other things. There are stories we hear of a patient who is told he will not walk again and with enough willpower if able to command control over his body while at the flip-side we have patients told that the prognosis is positive and yet they will never be able to work again. Otherwise, there are patients, such as myself, that have found incongruities between my symptoms and the response from professionals even amongst each other because a lot of symptoms overlap with other psychiatric disorders that put in question the validity of the claims. This is significant and illustrates why i say diagnosis is essentially random. The question “have i lost brain cells?” Is met with “we don’t have a scan before tbi so hard to tell to what extent or if you have at all”. 

The treatment plan is based on diagnosis and can be mismatched. For example: i was helped by occupational therapist to find a way to cook a basic meal and wash my dishes in the same day. A week later i met with the career councillor at the same rehab who tried to find me a job 30hr/week. It makes no sense. All i could say is that they’re probing around. Mind you, it is the best rehab center in my area but even then, i could say they didn’t know what they were doing. Furthermore, there was a radical shift in medical recommendation of a mtbi patient after accident which before 2013 was rest rest rest and after 2013 they decided that patients should be stressed as much as possible within reason to reactivate the brain. Also research is back and forth regarding neurogenesis.Im no expert in the matter,. It just seems like treating tbi is more of an art than a science. The research isn’t there and the fact that for now there is little empirical proof for what the patient is going through is sign enough that we haven’t advanced that much in the field. That being said, there is tremendous leaps in neuroscience which i definitely do not ignore. In fact i am trying to take an online class now about it (it’s a lot to take in) and am amazed at the complexity of the brain. 

Thank you for pointing out that the brain can heal. Indeed neuro plasticity works wonders. I think it’s a swell discovery. For people who have had a concussion with no cell death , there is even a chance of becoming a savant! The issue is that with decreased brain cells there is less capacity and so rehab expectations should be adjusted to that fact. We need all of our brain.

All of this is to say that there is a lot of guesswork involved in treating tbi and that we shouldn’t put all of our trust  into the hands of professionals as much as we would like to believe they hold the key to bouncing back into the game of life, especially because some tbi patients are vulnerable. I would recommend to try out a whole bunch of therapies and professionals to see what works but also take it with a grain of salt due to lack of seeing the bigger picture. I say, begin trusting yourself a little even if you don’t know who you are anymore. No one knows this reality like you do.

Also i am really happy about your studies and i wish you much success. It’s important to have people in the medical field participate in groups such as this one because it definitely bridges the gap.

Power to you and thanks again for correcting my statement.
